Operator: Good day, and welcome to the VeriCom Media Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. Today's conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to VeriCom Media's Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Jamie Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Patel, Chief Financial Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Network Officer; Lisa Moreno, Chief Commercial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.
Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Jamie Thompson: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I am excited to share our Q3 results, which reflect our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction. We achieved strong performance across several key areas.
First, our enterprise and B2B initiatives exceeded expectations with record bookings and key multi-year wins. Second, we continue to see strong adoption of our 5G Ultra Wideband plans, leading to meaningful ARPU uplift from bundling with premium streaming. Third, our focus on network expansion has yielded impressive 5G coverage gains and capacity improvements. Fourth, we are making significant strides in operational efficiencies through AI and Open RAN. Fifth, our efforts to optimize our balance sheet are paying off with deleveraging progress. Sixth, we are strategically investing in media convergence, and finally, we are exploring edge computing partnerships to drive future growth.

Sarah Patel: Thank you, Jamie. Now, let's move on to the financial results. Our revenue for the quarter reached $16.2 billion, an increase of 6% compared to the same period last year. Adjusted EBITDA was $6.3 billion, resulting in a margin of 38.8%. We are diligently managing our costs and optimizing our capital allocation. Capital expenditures amounted to $4.8 billion, primarily allocated to 5G infrastructure, fiber deployment, and content acquisition.
Good afternoon, everyone. As we look ahead, I'm pleased to provide our EBITDA margin guidance for the fourth quarter and full fiscal year 2025. Our EBITDA margins continue to reflect the resilience of our converged telecom and media platform, where we leverage our 5G fixed wireless access network and premium streaming content to drive both top-line growth and operational leverage.
For the fourth quarter of 2024, we are guiding to an adjusted EBITDA margin of 40% to 41%, representing a 110 to 140 basis point expansion sequentially from our Q3 reported margin. This puts us on track for full-year 2024 EBITDA margins of approximately 39.5%, up from 37.2% in FY 2023, driven by the structural improvements we've embedded across our business.
Looking further out to FY 2025, we expect adjusted EBITDA margins to expand to 41.5% to 43%, implying roughly 200 basis points of year-over-year growth at the midpoint. This guidance assumes consolidated revenue growth of 4% to 6%, with wireless service revenue up mid-single digits on 5G postpaid net adds of 1.2 to 1.5 million, broadband revenue growing 8% to 10% via FWA penetration exceeding 25% in our core U.S. markets, and media segment revenue accelerating to 7% growth on streaming ARPU expansion.
Let me break down the key drivers behind this margin trajectory, starting with the tailwinds. First, operational efficiencies and cost discipline remain our north star. We've realized over $450 million in run-rate opex savings year-to-date through our Network Lean initiative, which includes virtualizing 40% of our core RAN functions via Open RAN deployments with partners like Nokia and Rakuten Symphony. This has reduced site-related opex by 15% in greenfield 5G Standalone markets. Additionally, our AI-driven network orchestration platform—powered by our proprietary EdgeAI suite—has optimized traffic routing, cutting energy costs by 12% quarter-over-quarter amid rising power prices. We expect these efficiencies to contribute 150 to 200 basis points of margin expansion in FY 2025.
Second, pricing power and product mix shifts. In wireless, postpaid ARPU grew 2.8% year-over-year in Q3, fueled by our unlimited 5G Ultra plans bundled with our VeriStream+ service, which now boasts 18 million subscribers—up 25% YoY and capturing share from pure-play streamers like Netflix and Disney+. We're layering on premium tiers with 4K/HDR and ad-free options, targeting $15 ARPU uplift. In broadband, our fiber-to-the-home footprint reached 55% coverage in the Northeast U.S., enabling 10% pricing realization on gigabit plans. Media ad revenue is also inflecting positively, with connected TV impressions up 30% via integrations with Amazon Fire TV and Roku, outpacing industry growth as tracked by Nielsen.
Regionally, North America remains our margin powerhouse at 42% EBITDA margins in Q3, benefiting from spectrum efficiencies post our $2.2 billion C-band refill in FCC Auction 108. We're guiding to 43-44% margins here in FY 2025 as 5G SA coverage hits 85% of our top 100 MSAs. In Europe, where we operate through our 40% stake in EuroNet Mobile, margins are at 36% today but expected to expand 300 bps to 39% on 5G monetization and regulatory tailwinds from the EU's Gigabit Infrastructure Act, which accelerates pole attachments for our dark fiber JV with Crown Castle. Latin America, via our Mexican JV with Telefónica-inspired assets, is the growth engine at 32% margins but ramping to 35% on FWA adoption amid Claro's competitive dynamics—our 1 million sub target will leverage sub-$20/month pricing to drive 20% revenue growth.
Of course, we're not ignoring headwinds. Content costs in media remain elevated, with amortization from our $8 billion content library—including NFL Sunday Ticket rights akin to YouTube TV's deal—pressuring margins by 50 bps in Q4. We're mitigating this through windowing strategies and direct-to-consumer shifts, reducing wholesale video revenue declines to just 3% from double-digits. Inflationary pressures on capex, particularly tower leases and interconnect fees, add 30 bps of drag, though our capex intensity guidance of 16-18% of revenue—down from 20% in 2023—reflects disciplined spending, with 60% allocated to 5G Ultra Capacity and the rest to media cloud migration on AWS Outposts.
Strategically, M&A and partnerships are margin-accretive catalysts. The pending $3.5 billion acquisition of StreamForge, a CTV ad-tech platform similar to The Trade Desk, closes Q1 2025 and is expected to add 50 bps to margins via 20% EBITDA synergies from data clean rooms integrating our 150 million user IDs with telecom intent data. We're also deepening our edge computing JV with Microsoft Azure, targeting low-latency services for gaming and AR/VR, which could unlock $500 million in new high-margin enterprise revenue by FY 2026.
In summary, our FY 2025 EBITDA margin guidance of 41.5% to 43% underscores the power of our 5G-media convergence playbook, positioning us to outperform peers like T-Mobile on wireless margins and Comcast on converged EBITDA. We remain committed to returning 50-60% of free cash flow to shareholders via buybacks and our 4.2% dividend yield.
Before we open the line for Q&A, I'd like to provide a detailed update on our debt profile and leverage metrics, which remain a cornerstone of our capital structure amid the ongoing 5G ramp-up, streaming content wars, and fiber densification initiatives across our Telecom and Media segments. As you know, VeriCom Media's business model—blending wireless, broadband, and premium video streaming via our flagship VeriStream+ platform—requires disciplined balance sheet management to fund capex-intensive growth while delivering shareholder returns.
As of September 30, 2024, our gross debt stood at $48.2 billion, comprising $28 billion in long-term bonds—primarily investment-grade senior unsecured notes maturing 2026–2034—$12 billion in term loans and revolving credit facilities, $5.5 billion in tower financing leases under ASC 842, and $2.7 billion in short-term commercial paper. Net debt, after adjusting for $3.1 billion in cash and short-term investments, came in at $45.1 billion. This reflects a modest $1.2 billion increase quarter-over-quarter, driven largely by seasonal working capital needs and the funding of our $2.8 billion spectrum prepayments for the ongoing C-band auction Phase 2, echoing the FCC's aggressive mid-band push similar to what Verizon faced in 2021.
Turning to our key leverage metric, consolidated net Debt-to-EBITDA—calculated on a last-twelve-months trailing basis—was 2.7x at quarter-end, down from 2.9x in Q2 and a meaningful 21% improvement from 3.4x a year ago. This puts us comfortably within our target range of 2.5–3.0x, ahead of the BBB investment-grade threshold of around 3.5x, and positions us favorably against peers. For context, Verizon's leverage sits at ~2.6x, AT&T at 2.9x post-WarnerMedia spin, T-Mobile at a lean 2.4x thanks to Sprint synergies, and Comcast at 2.8x amid Peacock investments. In media pure-plays, Disney's at ~3.2x with ESPN+ DTC ramp, while Netflix hovers at a negative leverage due to FCF generation but lacks our capex drag.
We've deleveraged steadily since peaking at 4.1x in Q4 2021 amid COVID capex deferrals and the $15 billion acquisition of StreamForge Content Library, which bolstered our ad-supported tier now generating $1.2 billion in annual incremental AVOD revenue. Q3's improvement was fueled by 12% YoY EBITDA growth to $6.3 billion—LTM $19.2 billion—driven by wireless service revenue up 5% on postpaid ARPU expansion to $58.40 from 5G Ultra Wideband pricing, and Media segment EBITDA margins expanding 220 bps to 38% on linear-to-streaming mix shift.
Regionally, our U.S. operations—65% of EBITDA—maintain the strongest profile at 2.4x leverage, benefiting from rural digital opportunity subsidies—$1.1 billion RDOF tranche received YTD—and FTTH passings now at 45 million homes, rivaling Frontier's buildout pace. Europe, at 20% of EBITDA via our EuroNet Mobile JV stake and standalone ops in Germany/Italy, is at 3.1x due to higher euro-denominated debt yields post-ECB hikes, but we're mitigating via Open RAN trials with Nokia and Qualcomm, targeting 15–20% opex savings by 2025 to accelerate deleveraging. In APAC—India/Japan, 15% of EBITDA—leverage is 2.9x, supported by Jio-like 5G monetization with ARPU uplift of 18% YoY from JioAirFiber equivalents, though spectrum renewal costs in India added $800 million to debt this quarter.
Strategically, we're executing a multi-pronged deleveraging playbook tailored to telecom/media dynamics: Robust FCF generation—Q3 levered free cash flow hit $2.1 billion, up 25% YoY, with full-year guidance now $8.5–9.0 billion, enabling $3 billion in debt paydowns. This stems from EBITDA dollar growth outpacing capex, which we guided to $19.5 billion for 2024—24% of revenue—focused on 5G Standalone core upgrades and edge computing for low-latency streaming—critical as we integrate AI-driven personalization akin to Netflix's ecosystem.
Refinancing and maturity profile: Average debt cost is 4.1%, with 65% fixed-rate and no major maturities until 2026—$4.2 billion. We opportunistically refinanced $2 billion in 2023 notes at 150 bps below prior coupons, locking in sub-5% rates amid Fed pauses. Liquidity remains fortress-like at $10.2 billion, including $5 billion undrawn revolver.
Asset optimization: Tower monetization via our $1.5 billion sale-leaseback with Crown Castle closed earlier this year, with more master lease amendments planned. Media side, we're pruning non-core linear assets, targeting $500 million in proceeds from regional sports network divestitures amid Diamond Sports' bankruptcy ripple effects.
M&A discipline: Post-StreamForge, we're accretive-only on leverage, eyeing bolt-ons like regional MVNOs or content IP—similar to Liberty Media's Formula E play—that enhance 5G fixed wireless access bundles.
Forward-looking, we expect leverage to dip below 2.5x by year-end 2024 and 2.0x by 2026, assuming mid-single-digit revenue CAGR and EBITDA margins expanding to 42%. Risks include spectrum auction escalations or regulatory headwinds like the EU's DMA impacting ad tech, but our diversified footprint—wireless 45%, broadband 30%, media 25%—derisks us versus pure telco peers.
This balance sheet gives us optionality for buybacks—$4 billion authorized remaining—dividends—yield ~3.2%—and strategic investments in 6G R&D and metaverse streaming pilots.
As we wrap up a strong quarter with total revenue of $16.2 billion, up 6% year-over-year, and consolidated EBITDA of $6.3 billion at a 38.8% margin, I'm pleased to provide our forward-looking guidance on subscriber metrics and revenue growth. Our outlook reflects continued execution on our three-pillar strategy: accelerating 5G-Advanced and fiber broadband deployments, deepening media ecosystem integration through bundled streaming offerings, and optimizing ARPU via premium pricing and low-churn loyalty programs.
We ended Q3 with 58.2 million postpaid mobile subscribers, 24.7 million fiber broadband households, and 12.8 million paid streaming subscribers across our VeriStream platform and joint ventures. We're guiding for postpaid mobile subscriber net adds of 450,000 to 550,000 in Q4, implying total postpaid mobility subs of approximately 58.7 million by year-end—a sequential 0.8% growth and full-year net adds of 2.1 million, or 3.7% YoY expansion. This builds on our Q3 net adds of 520,000, driven by our 5G Ultra Wideband network now covering 95% of our top 100 U.S. markets and aggressive promotions around our Unlimited Max plan, which includes bundled access to ad-supported tiers of Disney+ and Max.
On the broadband side, expect fiber net adds of 350,000 to 450,000 in Q4, bringing our fiber footprint to 25.1 million households passed—up 8% sequentially from aggressive XGS-PON deployments in the Southeast and Midwest. Full-year fiber net adds will hit 1.6 million, representing 7% YoY growth, as we pass 30 million locations by YE2024. Churn remains industry-leading at 0.9% monthly, bolstered by our AI-powered network optimization reducing latency to under 10ms in 80% of fiber markets.
For streaming, we're targeting 200,000 to 300,000 net adds in Q4, growing to 13.1 million subs, with FY2024 full-year growth of 18% YoY. This is fueled by our VeriStream+ bundle, which now integrates Paramount+ Premium and our own FAST channels, achieving a 92% retention rate—well above the industry average amid ongoing cord-cutting pressures, where U.S. pay-TV households declined another 2% in Q3 per our Nielsen tracking.
For Q4, we expect total revenue of $16.1 billion to $16.4 billion, representing 2% to 4% sequential growth and 5% to 7% YoY. Service revenue—78% of the mix—should grow 3% QoQ to $12.7 billion, led by mobile service up 4% on 2% ARPU expansion to $55.50, driven by our family plan upselling and 5G mmWave upgrades. Broadband service revenue hits $4.2 billion, up 5% QoQ, with fiber ARPU climbing to $78 from residential gigabit adoption now at 65%. Wireless equipment revenue moderates to $2.1 billion on normalized iPhone 16 cycle pull-forward, while media and other revenue grows 12% to $1.4 billion, reflecting ad sales recovery on our CTV platform amid a soft but stabilizing upfront market.
For the full FY2025, we're raising our revenue outlook to $66.5 billion to $68.0 billion, implying 6% to 8% growth over FY2024's expected $62.9 billion. This incorporates mobile service revenue growth of 5% to 7%, reaching $27.5 billion, with ARPU stabilizing at $56+ via embedded 5G-Advanced features like carrier aggregation and edge AI for gaming/low-latency streaming. Broadband revenue expansion of 9% to 11% to $18.0 billion, as fiber penetration hits 40% in passed locations, outpacing cable peers like Comcast amid BEAD funding tailwinds in rural expansion. Media revenue acceleration to 15% growth at $6.2 billion, leveraging our 20% share of U.S. CTV ad impressions per Comscore and new partnerships, including a multi-year deal with Warner Bros. Discovery for HBO Max exclusives on VeriStream.
Regionally, U.S. operations—85% of revenue—drive the bulk of growth at 7% YoY, with California and Texas markets posting double-digit fiber gains. Europe, via our EuroNet Mobile JV, expects steady 3% subscriber growth amid regulatory spectrum auctions, while Latin America delivers 12% revenue upside from 5G monetization in Brazil and Mexico, offsetting Argentina's forex headwinds.
Strategically, this guidance embeds $2.5 billion in incremental capex for FY2025, focused on Open RAN trials with Nokia and Ericsson to cut SAC by 15%, and AI-driven content personalization to boost streaming engagement 25%. Risks include potential tariff impacts on device costs and competitive intensity from T-Mobile's pricing aggression, but our leading NPS of 72 and 1.2% blended churn position us for outperformance.
We remain committed to mid-30% EBITDA margins and $10 billion in FY2025 free cash flow to support our $0.65 quarterly dividend and $5 billion share repurchase authorization.

Mike Chen: Thank you, Sarah. I would like to provide an update on our network performance and expansion. We continue to enhance our 5G network, achieving wider coverage and faster speeds. Our network reliability remains high, and we are investing in advanced technologies to further improve performance. We are also focused on optimizing our network for emerging applications like IoT and edge computing.
Before I dive deeper into the financials, I'd like to spend a few minutes on one of our highest-priority areas: network investments, with a specific focus on our 5G deployment progress and the associated capital expenditures. In the hyper-competitive Telecommunications and Media landscape, 5G isn't just an upgrade—it's the foundational enabler for next-gen services like ultra-low-latency streaming, immersive AR/VR media experiences, and edge computing for content delivery networks. We're executing aggressively here to maintain our leadership position against peers like Verizon, AT&T, and T-Mobile, while unlocking synergies with our media assets, including VeriStream+ and our growing CDN partnerships.
In Q3, we deployed capex of $4.8 billion, up 12% year-over-year, with approximately 42%—or $2.0 billion—directly allocated to 5G network enhancements. This brings our year-to-date capex to $13.7 billion, on track with our full-year guidance of $19.5 billion to $20.5 billion. Of that, we expect 38-40% to fund 5G initiatives, reflecting a deliberate shift from our 2022 mix where 5G capex was closer to 30%. This moderation from peak spending levels—down from $22 billion in 2021 during our initial C-band spectrum rollout—demonstrates disciplined capital allocation as we transition from buildout to optimization and monetization phases.
I'm pleased to report robust progress on our 5G Standalone architecture, which now covers 92% of our top 100 U.S. metro markets, up from 85% at year-end 2023. Overall population coverage stands at 88% for sub-6GHz 5G—our workhorse for broad mid-band capacity—and we've achieved 65% coverage in high-traffic urban and suburban areas with C-band spectrum, acquired at the 2021 FCC auction for $3.7 billion. This positions us ahead of the industry average, per Ookla's latest Speedtest Intelligence report, where our median 5G download speeds hit 285 Mbps, a 22% improvement quarter-over-quarter.
Technically, we've upgraded over 28,000 macro sites with massive MIMO Active Antennas—primarily Nokia AirScale and Ericsson Massive MIMO radios—delivering up to 4x capacity gains per site. Densification remains key: We've installed 52,000 small cells and Distributed Antenna Systems in the quarter, focused on stadiums, malls, and enterprise campuses. A notable initiative is our Open RAN pilot in the Southeast, where we've deployed 1,200 radios from Altiostar and Parallel Wireless, achieving 15-20% OpEx savings on integration versus traditional proprietary RAN. This aligns with the industry's ORAN momentum, as seen in DISH Network's aggressive adoption and the O-RAN Alliance's growing ecosystem.
On the core side, 85% of our 5G traffic now runs on our cloud-native 5G SA core, leveraging Ericsson's dual-mode 5G Core platform. This enables network slicing for media use cases—like prioritized low-latency slices for VeriStream+'s 8K live sports streaming and gaming partnerships with Epic Games. We've also densified backhaul with 15,000 miles of new fiber, addressing a critical bottleneck; fiber now backhauls 92% of our 5G sites, up from 78% last year, in line with trends from peers like Crown Castle and American Tower.
Regionally, performance varies but trends positively: U.S. Urban Core—e.g., NYC, LA, Chicago—98% sub-6 coverage, 75% mmWave in dense pockets for gigabit speeds. mmWave deployments—using Samsung and Qualcomm chips—now serve 15 million passings, powering fixed wireless access pilots with 500 Mbps symmetrical speeds. Suburban and Secondary Markets: 90% coverage, with a focus on mid-band C-band to compete with T-Mobile's extended range. ARPU uplift here is already +8% from 5G Unlimited plans. Rural Expansion: Through our Enhanced Airborne Network partnerships with AST SpaceMobile, we've begun satellite-integrated 5G trials covering 20% of rural POCs, mitigating the $2-3 million per site cost of traditional towers. This is crucial as rural broadband subsidies from the $42.5 billion BEAD program ramp up. International—Europe and LatAm: In our Spanish and Brazilian footprints via JV with Telefónica, we've hit 75% 5G coverage in Madrid and São Paulo, leveraging n78 band spectrum for media-heavy markets.
Strategically, our 5G investments are yielding tangible returns. Postpaid 5G subscriber adds reached 1.2 million in Q3—45% of total net adds—with blended ARPU at $58, up 4% YoY, driven by premium 5G plans bundled with ad-free VeriStream+ streaming. Churn remains low at 0.92%, best-in-class, as 5G reliability boosts customer satisfaction scores to 78 on the ACSI index.
We're also capitalizing on media convergence: 5G edge computing nodes—now 2,500 deployed with AWS Wavelength—reduce latency for our CDN to under 10ms, enabling 360-degree video and cloud gaming. This ties directly to our content ecosystem; Q3 5G video traffic grew 35% YoY, accounting for 28% of total data usage, per our internal Deep Packet Inspection analytics.
Looking ahead, capex intensity—as a percentage of revenue—will peak at 18% this year before declining to 15-16% in 2025, as ROI accelerates. We forecast 5G to contribute $2.5 billion in incremental EBITDA by 2026 through higher ARPU—+$5/postpaid line—FWA broadband—targeting 2 million subs—and enterprise private networks—e.g., slicing for NFL stadiums and manufacturing IoT. Risks include supply chain pressures on semiconductors—we've secured 18 months of Qualcomm X-series modems—and regulatory hurdles like the ongoing net neutrality debates, but our spectrum position—280 MHz average—de-risks this.
In summary, our 5G network is not just deployed—it's transforming our Telecom and Media franchises into a converged powerhouse. We're on pace for industry-leading coverage and efficiency, setting the stage for sustainable free cash flow growth.

Lisa Moreno: Thank you, Mike. I'm excited to share our commercial achievements. We saw strong growth in subscriber additions, driven by our innovative product offerings and targeted marketing campaigns. Customer satisfaction remains a top priority, and we are continuously working to improve the customer experience across all touchpoints. We are also focused on expanding our partnerships to offer bundled services and enhance customer value.
I'll now turn to our Enterprise and B2B segment, which continues to be a cornerstone of our growth strategy here at VeriCom Media. As you know, this segment leverages our world-class fiber backbone, 5G Standalone core, and media delivery expertise to deliver mission-critical solutions for enterprises—from private 5G networks and SD-WAN overlays to edge computing platforms and low-latency content delivery networks. In a market where Gartner projects global enterprise telecom spend to exceed $1.2 trillion by 2025, driven by hybrid cloud adoption and Industry 4.0, we're executing aggressively on our Connect & Compute initiative.
In Q3, Enterprise and B2B revenues hit $1.45 billion, up 32% year-over-year and 8% quarter-over-quarter—well ahead of our guided 25-30% full-year growth target. This represents 28% of our total service revenues, with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding 450 basis points to 42%, thanks to higher-margin recurring services like managed 5G slicing and AI-optimized network orchestration. Average revenue per user in this segment climbed 18% to $1,250 per month, fueled by multi-year contracts bundling connectivity with our EdgeMedia platform, which now processes over 10 petabytes of enterprise data daily with sub-5ms latency.
Pipeline visibility remains robust at $28 billion—up 45% YoY—with a weighted close probability of 62%. Bookings in the quarter totaled $2.1 billion, a record, including 75% from new logos and expansions. Contract duration averaged 48 months, with 65% structured as SaaS-like recurring revenue, insulating us from cyclical pressures.
Now, onto key wins, which underscore our momentum across verticals and regions: North America—65% of bookings: Our crown jewel was a $750 million, 5-year deal with a top-3 U.S. retailer—think Walmart-scale—to deploy private 5G networks across 1,200 warehouses and stores. This includes our uRLLC slices for AR-guided picking and robotics automation, integrated with their SAP ERP via our 5G MEC nodes. Early results? 35% faster inventory throughput and 20% reduction in fulfillment errors. We also expanded our partnership with a leading hyperscaler—modeled after AWS Outposts—securing a $400 million follow-on for hybrid edge-cloud services, powering their generative AI inference at the edge.
Europe—22% of bookings: Amid the EU's Gigabit Society push and ongoing spectrum auctions, we inked a €320 million—or $350 million—contract with a major automotive OEM, akin to Volkswagen, for a campus-wide 5G private network at their Wolfsburg Gigafactory. This features RedCap IoT for connected vehicle testing and our Network Digital Twin platform, which uses AI/ML for predictive maintenance—reducing downtime by 28% in pilots. Regulatory tailwinds here are strong; our CBRS-like shared spectrum advocacy in the UK and Germany has positioned us for the upcoming 6GHz unlicensed band opening.
APAC—13% of bookings: We broke into Japan with a ¥45 billion—or $300 million—win alongside NTT Docomo for a smart city rollout in Yokohama, delivering eMBB for 4K/8K media streaming on digital signage networks. This taps into the region's $50 billion verticals market, per IDC, with our MediaEdge CDN handling 5G-optimized AV1 codec transcoding for ultra-low bitrate efficiency.
Technically, we're ahead on several fronts. Our 5G SA core now supports network slicing for 500+ enterprise profiles, with end-to-end automation via ONAP-compliant orchestration—cutting deployment times from 6 months to 6 weeks. We've also rolled out our Quantum-Safe Encryption suite across all B2B traffic, addressing rising cyber threats in media supply chains, post the recent MGM ransomware incident. Partnerships with Nokia for O-RAN integration and Cisco for SD-WAN have accelerated our Time-to-Market.
Strategically, we're laser-focused on three pillars: Vertical specialization—healthcare, e.g., telemedicine slicing pilots with Cleveland Clinic analogs; manufacturing, CBAM-compliant sustainability tracking; and media/entertainment, dynamic ad insertion for enterprise streaming, rivaling Akamai's reach. M&A adjacency—post our acquisition of EdgeNet last year, we're eyeing bolt-on RAN software plays to capture 15% share in the $40 billion private 5G market by 2027, per ABI Research. And sustainability integration—all new contracts include net-zero path commitments, aligning with Scope 3 emissions reporting under CSRD/CSF frameworks.
Looking ahead, we see Q4 bookings accelerating to $2.4-$2.6 billion, with enterprise ARPU trending toward $1,400. Risks? Supply chain for mmWave gear and capex intensity, but our $5.2 billion 2024 capex plan—40% allocated here—de-risks delivery via domestic manufacturing ramps.
In summary, Enterprise and B2B isn't just growing—it's transforming VeriCom Media into the go-to 5G-media-edge partner.
As we dive into the financials further, I'd like to focus on one of our key performance metrics: ARPU, or Average Revenue Per User. Our disciplined execution on pricing discipline and innovative bundling strategies continues to drive meaningful ARPU uplift, offsetting regulatory headwinds and competitive intensity in a maturing post-pandemic market. Let me break this down with specifics across segments, regions, and YoY comparisons.
Consolidated blended ARPU reached $58.47 in Q3, marking a robust 5.8% YoY increase from $55.26 last year—a $3.21 absolute dollar uplift. This exceeds our internal guidance of 4-5% and reflects the full-quarter impact of our mid-year pricing actions, which we rolled out selectively across 65% of our postpaid mobile base and 80% of our fixed broadband subscribers. Excluding one-time COVID-era promotional offsets from Q3 '22, the underlying organic growth was even stronger at 6.2%.
Let's segment this out for clarity: Mobile Postpaid ARPU: $48.32, up 4.1% YoY or $1.90 higher. This was propelled by our tiered pricing strategy, where we implemented 5-7% increases on unlimited plans, particularly our Ultra 5G tier, which now accounts for 42% of postpaid adds—up from 28% a year ago. 5G Standalone core deployment across 75% of our U.S. footprint has enabled premium add-ons like 5G Advanced with mmWave for fixed wireless access trials, contributing $0.45 to the uplift. Family plans saw bundling with our VeriStream service—our ad-supported streaming JV with Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery—driving a 12% ARPU premium for multi-line households.
Fixed Broadband ARPU: A standout at $72.15, surging 7.2% YoY or $4.83 higher. Here, pricing was more aggressive: 8-10% hikes on DOCSIS 3.1 speeds above 1Gbps, aligned with inflation and capex recovery from our XGS-PON fiber overbuild, now passing 45 million homes. Bundling with mobile delivered a 15% ARPU lift for converged 'quad-play' customers—video + broadband + mobile + streaming—reducing churn to sub-1% monthly—best-in-class versus Comcast's 1.2% or Charter's 1.4%.
Video/Streaming ARPU—standalone metric for our 18 million subs: $14.20, up 9.5% YoY or $1.23, fueled by our 'VeriFlex' bundles integrating Peacock Premium, ESPN+, and local sports RSNs. Sports rights inflation was a tailwind; we locked in NBA and NFL carriage deals at favorable economics, adding $0.67 per sub from dynamic pricing during playoffs.
Blended ARPU excludes prepaid, which grew users 3% but held flat at $28.50 due to value-oriented plans in emerging markets—more on regions shortly.
Pricing Strategy Deep Dive: We took measured price increases totaling $450 million in annualized revenue run-rate, targeting low-elasticity segments like high-usage postpaid and fiber customers. Elasticity testing pre-launch showed <1% churn impact, validated post-rollout at 0.7%. This mirrors Verizon's successful 2023 playbook but with our edge in converged services, where 62% of price-affected customers opted into bundles rather than downgrade.
Bundling Impact: The real ARPU accelerator. Our 'OneCom' ecosystem—mobile + fixed + streaming—now serves 28 million households, up 22% YoY, delivering a $12.40 blended ARPU premium over single-play users. Cross-sell penetration hit 35% in Q3, with AI-driven recommendations via our customer app boosting take-rates by 18%. For example, bundling VeriStream with 5G Home Internet yields 25% higher lifetime value than standalone FWA, akin to T-Mobile's Go5G bundling success but with superior fiber economics.
Regional Commentary: North America—72% of revenue: U.S. ARPU at $62.10 (+6.3% YoY), Canada at $54.80 (+4.9%). Fiber expansion in Sun Belt markets countered cord-cutting, with ARPU uplift from Spectrum-like video bundles. Europe—18%: $51.20 (+3.2% YoY), tempered by EuroNet Mobile merger synergies and EU roaming caps. UK and Germany saw 5% pricing wins via Virgin Media O2-style converged offers. APAC/LATAM—10%: $42.75 (+7.1% YoY), led by India prepaid bundles with Jio-like data + Disney+ Hotstar, and Brazil fiber pricing amid Vivo's competitive push.
Forward-looking, we expect Q4 consolidated ARPU growth of 5-6% YoY, with full-year at 5.2%, supporting our raised 2024 EBITDA guidance to $25.5-26 billion. Risks include FCC net neutrality reviews and Dish/T-Mobile spectrum auctions, but our 5G mid-band leadership—280 MHz avg.—positions us for sustained pricing power.

Mike Chen: Great question, Emily. We're deploying EdgeAI across our 5G core for predictive traffic management, already cutting energy opex by 12% QoQ. This, combined with Open RAN virtualization, targets 150-200 bps margin expansion in FY25, directly feeding into Sarah's guidance.

Net neutrality risks are mitigated by our premium service focus, and EU Gigabit Act tailwinds support Europe growth—overall, regulatory dynamics favor our converged model.
